title: A run that spells COFFEE
prompt: Write a GPX file for a running route through Melbourne's CBD whose GPS trace spells COFFEE. It has to be a route someone could actually run: along the streets, not through the buildings.

oldPrompts.prompt: Write a GPX file for a running route through Melbourne's CBD whose GPS trace spells COFFEE.
oldPrompts.why: The first wording never said the route had to follow streets, so a trace drawn straight across the blocks was not actually answering the question wrongly. Two runs went out under it on 2026-09-15 and the wording was tightened the next day. Neither of those runs was ever published, so nothing on the board was scored against this version. It is recorded anyway, because a prompt that changes without a record is not a frozen prompt, and this change went unrecorded until 2026-09-21, when a check started diffing every published wording against the runs that used it.

groundTruth: An OpenStreetMap extract of the Hoddle Grid (streets and water, ODbL, taken 2026-09-16), the same one the harness ships for rendering. Every track point is measured to the nearest street centreline.

checks.label: On real streets
checks.how: Share of track points within 25 m of a mapped street centreline.

checks.label: One continuous route
checks.how: A single track segment, with no jump between consecutive points bigger than a city block.

checks.label: Inside the grid
checks.how: The whole trace sits within the Hoddle Grid, and does not cross the Yarra.

checks.label: Metadata true
checks.how: The streets the file's own description names are the streets the trace actually uses.
checks.rule: Pass if every street the file's description names is one the trace runs along for at least a block, read off the map under the trace. One named street the route never uses fails it.

checks.label: Reads as COFFEE
checks.how: Six letters recognisable from the plotted trace without being told what to look for.
checks.rule: Pass if the six letters can be read off the plotted trace in order, by someone not told the word first. In practice that someone is me, and I knew the word, which is the weakness of this check.

harder: Spell it without retracing any street twice, so the letters cannot be drawn as out-and-back arms.
